svg.font-family: ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace
svg.title: Bayu Indoor on the Bayu Core board
svg.desc: Connector map of the planned Bayu Core carrier board as fitted for the Indoor role: the PMS5003 on the 8-pin PicoBlade, the SCD40 and SHT40 on the two Grove I2C sockets, the XIAO ESP32-S3 in its socket. Nets are named at every pin instead of drawn as traces.
svg.text: Bayu Indoor on the Bayu Core board (phase 1)
A connector map for the board, drawn before any PCB layout. Pins with the same net name share copper.
test pads on SDA, SCL, TX, RX, 5V_F, 3V3, GND
A PicoBlade cable can be crimped 1-to-1 or 1-to-8. With the
sensor unplugged, beep J1 pin 1 through to the sensor's pin 1.
A flipped cable leaves the PMS unpowered and puts D6 on its
TXD pin, so check it once per cable.
Grove VCC on J2, J3 and J5 is 3V3 on this board, not 5 V.
Grove and breakout boards for the SCD40 and SHT40 usually
bring 10 kΩ pull-ups each. Two on the bus give 5 kΩ.
Close JP1 only for a bare sensor or the SEN54 on its own
UART names follow the XIAO: UART_RX is the PMS TXD going into D7, UART_TX leaves D6 for the PMS RXD.
